transcript.text: Alright everyone, thanks for being here. As we kick off this pre-show approval meeting for the live comedy special at the Orpheum on September 14th, I want to go around the room. We've got a draft plan on the table that uses a rotating scenic unit, an online replay, two audience blocks, and live audience questions. Before I issue final approval, I need to hear from each of you — technical, legal, insurance, and talent — on any operational requirements or concerns you have. Let's start with technical.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical technical issue. During this week's load test, I measured the Orpheum's loading-dock lift and it has a hard 900-kilogram limit. Our drafted rotating scenic unit weighs 1,100 kilograms, which exceeds that by 200 kilos. The good news is that splitting it into two 550-kilogram modules is workable and would get us under the limit. However, I haven't updated the load-in drawing yet to reflect the two-module approach, so I'll need to do that before we finalize.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a rights clearance issue. I confirmed with the archive licensor yesterday that the special's historical comedy clips are cleared for the theater recording and domestic broadcast, but they are NOT cleared for online replay. The current draft plan includes an online replay, which would put us in violation of our licensing terms. I also need to disclose that I have not yet entered this restriction in the distribution worksheet, so it's not reflected there. We'll need to either remove the online replay from the plan or secure additional clearance before final approval.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical insurance requirement. I obtained the insurer's written event endorsement this morning, and it requires that the audience be seated in three blocks separated by two unobstructed aisles, each at least 1.2 meters wide, for our coverage to remain valid. Our current draft plan seats the audience in only two blocks, which would put us in violation of the endorsement and jeopardize our insurance coverage. I should also note that the endorsement is still attached to my email rather than the production file, so it hasn't been formally uploaded to our records yet. We'll need to revise the seating plan to three blocks with the required aisle spacing before final approval.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical talent restriction. I confirmed with the comedian's representative this week that the comedian's approved participation permits moderated questions submitted before the show, but does NOT permit unscripted live audience questions. Our current draft plan includes live audience questions, which would violate the terms of the comedian's participation agreement. I should also disclose that I have not yet added this format restriction to the talent call sheet, so it's not reflected there. We'll need to replace the live audience questions with a moderated, pre-submitted question format before final approval.
